ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are two vertical blue straight lines; the left one passes through points Q and T, and the right one passes through points R and S. From point Q to point R there is a line segment slanting downward to the right, and from point T to point S there is also a line segment slanting downward to the right. The problem gives QR ∥ TS, QT ∥ RS. Angle 1 and angle 2 are adjacent at point Q, respectively located on the upper and lower sides of the slanted line QR, and together they form a straight angle along the straight line QT. Angle 5 is at point R, located between the two vertical parallel lines and on the other side of the slanted line QR. Reasoning: Because ∠1 and ∠2 are a pair of linear adjacent angles, m∠1 + m∠2 = 180°. Given m∠1 = 131°, therefore m∠2 = 180° - 131° = 49°. Also because QT ∥ RS, and QR is a transversal, ∠2 and ∠5 are located between the two parallel lines and on opposite sides of the transversal QR, so they are alternate interior angles, and their measures are equal. Therefore m∠5 = 49°.
